policy_assumptions.label: National reference prices apply to providers accepting federal money
Every resident is automatically enrolled in catastrophic coverage
Subsidies are calculated from income and household status
Private insurance becomes optional supplemental coverage

model_assumptions.label: Target government health spending as share of GDP
Target total health spending as share of GDP
Share of theoretical savings actually achieved
Transition cost offset as a share of gross annual government savings

rollout_sequence.label: Transparent national prices
rollout_sequence.description: Set the price foundation before asking households to use accounts.

rollout_sequence.label: Automated payment and eligibility rail
rollout_sequence.description: Build the IDs, ledger, income feed, claims clearing, and audit system first.

rollout_sequence.label: Universal catastrophic insurance
rollout_sequence.description: Protect people from major costs before routine spending shifts into accounts.

rollout_sequence.label: Automatic income-based subsidies
rollout_sequence.description: Replace enrollment churn with automatic top-ups and premium support.

rollout_sequence.label: Mandatory health savings
rollout_sequence.description: Require savings only after prices and catastrophic coverage are already in place.

rollout_sequence.label: Medicaid and ACA conversion
rollout_sequence.description: Convert existing support into top-ups, premium help, and safety-net support over time.

rollout_sequence.label: Private insurance as supplemental coverage
rollout_sequence.description: Move private insurance from core coverage to optional upgrades.

rollout_sequence.label: Retirement reform later
rollout_sequence.description: Do not bundle full Social Security replacement into the first health bill.

safeguards_model.headline: Your system needs three hard gates: identity, price, and claims.

account_formula.label: Account identity rule
account_formula.expression: Account_i = VerifiedID_i + Income_i + HealthStatus_i + VeteranStatus_i + SurvivorStatus_i

payment_formula.label: Provider payment rule
payment_formula.expression: Payment = ApprovedService x NationalPrice x MedicalNecessityScore

audit_formula.label: Audit priority rule
audit_formula.expression: AuditPriority_i = ClaimSize_i x RiskScore_i x ProviderOutlierScore_i

account_rules.title: One person, one account
account_rules.description: Each person gets one APAS account tied to verified identity, income, health, veteran, and survivor status.

account_rules.title: Restricted health funds
account_rules.description: Health money behaves like a restricted card and cannot be withdrawn as cash.

account_safeguards.guardrail: No cash withdrawal for health funds

provider_controls.fix: Compare provider billing patterns against peers
Require patient confirmation for routine claims
Flag abnormal volume per patient and provider

foundation_points: Safety net after account, insurance, and subsidy
boost_controls: Do not accept self-reported disability, survivor, or veteran boosts.
Keep the system generous for real need but hard to game.

dashboard_model.mixed_year_note: Spending is anchored to 2024 CMS baseline values. Population and demographic shares use the newest complete official 2024 Census-based inputs.

covered_for_everyone.coverage_level: Covered with low or no copay

hard_truth_requirements: Catastrophic coverage instead of full first-dollar coverage
Need boosts only through verified eligibility
dashboard_model.system_pitch: The system guarantees basic healthcare, catastrophic protection, retirement support, veteran boosts, disability protection, and survivor support. It does not guarantee unlimited provider choice, unlimited brand-name drugs, or unlimited billing at private-sector prices.
